title: Ek number do phone pe? iPhone Handoff kaise kaam karta hai?
hooks: Do iPhone, ek number? Handoff magic.
Phone number ab portable hai. Dekho kaise.
hook_why: Opens with Hindi hook word 'Ek' at frame 0, instant curiosity about one number on two phones, colloquial Hinglish, no greeting. Visual: two iPhones with a glowing number traveling between them on a digital highway — matches top Shorts' relay-baton metaphor.
metaphor: Digital highway: the phone number is a glowing data car that drives on a neon highway between two iPhone destinations. The highway lights up only when the target iPhone is unlocked.
mechanism: Same Apple Account on both devices
Bluetooth and Wi-Fi turned on for each device
Handoff enabled in Settings > General > AirPlay & Continuity
Devices within 30 feet (10 meters) of each other
Carrier eSIM that supports number sharing (T-Mobile US, Telekom Germany, EE UK)
One iPhone becomes Main, the other Secondary sharing the number
Unlock the iPhone you want to use — number switches automatically
Number active on only one iPhone at a time; arrow icon on old device, 'Switched to this iPhone' on new
Apple Watch stays paired to Main iPhone

fresh_fixed: scene 2: claims 'iOS 27 ka naya iPhone Handoff feature' -> Handoff is an existing Continuity feature, not a new iOS 27 addition according to the latest sources.

scene 3: lists 'MESSAGES IN ICLOUD' and 'FaceTime' as required -> latest sources state the only requirements are Same Apple Account, Bluetooth on, Wi‑Fi on, Handoff enabled, and devices within 30 ft; Messages in iCloud and FaceTime are not required.

steps_learned: Enable Handoff in Settings > General > AirPlay & Continuity
Ensure both iPhones have the same Apple ID, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth on
Use a carrier that supports eSIM (T-Mobile, Telekom, EE)
Designate one phone as Main and the other as Secondary to share the number
Unlock the desired phone to switch the active number
Observe the arrow icon indicating where the number is currently active
missing_steps: Explanation of what eSIM is and why physical SIM cards cannot be shared this way
Clarification that this feature is not available for all carriers or regions (specifically missing Indian carrier context)
Explanation of how to initially set up the 'Secondary' phone status in the phone settings
